_file: Scenarios for response-side identity binding. The audit gateway has already done the inspection (audit-gateway.mjs inspectIdentity) and hands the collector an `identity` block plus `quarantined`/`failureClass`; these scenarios pin what the collector must DO with them.
_windowNote: fromDate is non-zero throughout: a window starting at epoch 0 cannot receive the mandated 1ms lower-bound expansion and therefore carries LOG_WINDOW_LOWER_BOUND_UNEXPANDED, which would drown out the identity assertions these scenarios exist for.

record-without-location.why: Plan line 438: absence records bindingMethod 'request_scope'. That is a weaker claim than a native match but it is still evidence, so the events must be RETAINED and the window may still be complete - downgrading absence to a failure would make most of this API unreadable.

record-with-native-location.planBullet: Returned record without a locationId (contrast case)
record-with-native-location.why: The contrast that makes the request_scope scenario meaningful. When every read carried and matched a native identity the binding method must say 'native', otherwise 'request_scope' is just a constant and proves nothing.

mixed-binding-methods-across-components.planBullet: Returned record without a locationId (mixed case)
mixed-binding-methods-across-components.why: 'mixed' is the value REAL responses will overwhelmingly produce - some routes echo a locationId and some do not - and no fixture generated it, so the whole mixed branch was untested and a mutant collapsing it to 'native' or 'request_scope' survived. Here the log route binds natively while every other read binds by request scope, which is exactly the shape of a live run.

record-with-conflicting-location.why: Plan line 439: a conflicting identity QUARANTINES, it does not degrade to Partial. The gateway already returns ok:false + quarantined:true; the collector must drop the payload from the evidence set rather than merge another location's rows into this location's runtime window, and must say the window is not complete.

identity-inspection-capped.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (incompleteness sibling)
identity-inspection-capped.why: Task 2 carry-forward item 6: inspectionCapped and depthCapped return ok:false and must map to complete:false, NEVER to empty. A capped inspection means the guard switched itself off inside a legal page - the rows may be another location's and nothing proved otherwise. locationBinding.inspectionIncomplete must SAY so; it was never asserted anywhere, so a mutant that never set it survived.

identity-depth-capped.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (incompleteness sibling)
identity-depth-capped.why: The depth-capped half of carry-forward item 6. Recorded on its own flag by the gateway because the operator response differs, but the verdict for the collector is identical: not a read.

identity-unreadable.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (incompleteness sibling)
identity-unreadable.why: IDENTITY_UNREADABLE is the third of the three incompleteness classes and the only one whose signal reaches the collector through `identity.unreadable` rather than a boolean flag. Without a fixture, the `(identity.unreadable ?? []).length > 0` arm of the inspectionIncomplete test was never executed.

component-auth-refused.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (fail-closed sibling)
component-auth-refused.why: A 403 latches NOTHING on the shared circuit by design (carry-forward, circuit scoping), so the run continues and the OTHER components still read cleanly. The refused component must be recorded as incomplete rather than as an empty per-step count set, which would read as a workflow nobody is sitting in.

definition-read-refused.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (fail-closed sibling)
definition-read-refused.why: The `if (!detail.ok) warnForFailure(...)` guard on the three definition reads had no fixture at all, so deleting it survived: the definition would come back as three nulls with the window still complete:true. A definition that could not be read must also null the canonical hash - Task 7 binds a receipt to that hash, and a partial definition hashing to a complete-looking value would bind a receipt to evidence nobody collected.

trigger-read-refused.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (fail-closed sibling)
trigger-read-refused.why: Each of the three definition reads needs its OWN refusal case. With only the detail read covered, dropping `if (!triggersResponse.ok) warnForFailure(...)` survives: the trigger list comes back null, the canonical hash is correctly null, but the FAILURE itself is never reported, so an auditor sees a definition with no triggers and no stated reason - which reads as a workflow nothing can start.

sticky-note-read-refused.planBullet: Returned record with conflicting locationId (fail-closed sibling)
sticky-note-read-refused.why: The third definition read's refusal guard, for the same reason as the trigger one. A sticky-note read that was refused must not present as a workflow whose author left no notes.

unreadable-definition-envelopes.planBullet: Returned record without a locationId (envelope guard)
unreadable-definition-envelopes.why: Both the trigger and sticky-note responses come back ok:true with an envelope naming no array. rowsOf must return null, definitionComplete must be false, and the canonical hash must be null. Under the `return []` mutant all three read as an empty-but-successful definition, and the hash would be computed over two arrays that were never observed.
